title: ADM reviewer decision (adm-review-result/v1)
description: The only thing that can authorize completing a reviewed candidate. A reviewer returns this as a ```adm-review-result fenced block (or as native structured output). Shape alone never authorizes: manager/nextplan/contracts.py review_authority additionally binds target_sha to the candidate ADM is holding and reviewer_run_id/provenance to the reviewer run ADM itself dispatched, and with no dispatch record on file nothing can authorize. Prose in the same message is explanation and may withdraw a PASS it contradicts, but can never grant one. Round 6: the object is CLOSED. It was additionalProperties:true, and a PASS carrying blocking:true, required_action:"repair", status:"needs_changes" or can_merge:false validated and completed the task, because an unknown key was silently dropped. Dropping a key is only safe when the key cannot have been decision-bearing, which is exactly what an unknown key does not establish. An additive extension is therefore a reviewed change to this contract, not a new field name an agent can invent. Prose in the same message may also now CONFLICT with the object: a second explicit decision statement ("Current decision: reject", "I reject this"), or a decision field whose value ADM cannot read, makes the pair a conflict and blocks.

target_sha.description: The exact commit reviewed. Must be the candidate ADM is holding; a decision about any other commit is irrelevant and neither authorizes nor blocks.

reviewer_run_id.description: The run identity ADM issued when it dispatched this review. This is the field a forger cannot supply.

verdict.description: Absent, empty and unrecognised values are all INVALID and block. They are never read as silence.

findings.description: Required. An empty list is the positive statement that there are none. A PASS carrying any blocking finding is a contradiction and blocks.

severity.description: Omitted means blocking: an unreadable severity is not a harmless one.

mode.description: A reviewer that could write is not an independent reviewer (AI-DEVELOPMENT-RULES 32).

summary.description: Optional prose for humans. Carries no authority.
